_: The controlled genres & moods vocabulary (DT-B, from DT-taxonomy.md) — four orthogonal axes the classify pass assigns from. `scripts/v2/combined_questions.py` reads it, builds one question per label from it, and hashes this file into every shard manifest as `taxonomySha256`; `scripts/genres_moods_enrich.py` holds `data/genres-moods-definitions.json` to exactly these labels. Every label is written once, here.

notes.version: What a bump reclassifies against: recorded as `taxonomyVersion` in every shard manifest, in the shipped labels file and in `data/genres-moods-curated.json`, and split from `embeddingModelVersion` so the two move independently.
notes.primaryGenres: Exactly one per title (the "Drama is too broad" fix) — 17 TMDB genres. `Animation` is excluded: it is a medium, not a story genre, and is carried separately by the `animated` flag (TMDB genre 16). An animated title is classified by its underlying story genre (Toy Story → Adventure), so it can sit in both an "Animated" row (from the flag) and its genre rows.
notes.thematic: Thematic labels. `Narco`, `Giallo`, `Hong Kong Action` and `Samurai` are emergent — clustering the on-device vectors found them as cohesive groups the seed vocabulary missed. They are content-detectable, so they are themes a model may assign rather than recipe-only regional labels. (`Telenovela` was dropped in t02 — 5 titles, dead.) t02 also added anime and the thematic/interest labels Netflix has and we lacked; `Cult`, `Anime`, `Art House` and `Epic` lean on world knowledge rather than on the plot, so a plot-only model should omit them (DT-prompt).
notes.regional: Regional labels (origin/language; mostly recipe-driven, stored for consistency). No question is built from these — they describe where a title comes from, which is metadata rather than something to infer from prose.
notes.moods: Mood/tone — the model's main value-add, since TMDB cannot express these.
notes.deduplication: One spelling per label, across families as well as within one: "Western" is a primary genre only (dropped as a theme), and "Courtroom" folds into "Legal/Courtroom Drama" rather than standing as its own theme. `combined_questions.taxonomy()` refuses a repeat.
